item.title: Criticism of LGBTQ+ raids in Turkey is growing
item.description: Several raids and arrests of LGBTQ+ persons in Turkey have triggered sharp criticism from numerous Turkish organizations — and also from Brussels.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Why do authoritarian regimes target the LGBTQ+ community?
item.description: A recent crackdown on the LGBTQ+ community in Turkey is symptomatic of a wider rights regression, according to experts. It's worse under authoritarian regimes, but why is it such a popular policy for these states?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Saudi Arabia faces hard choices as Houthis gain in Yemen
item.description: Saudi Arabia faces growing security and economic problems as it seeks to balance deterrence and diplomacy during its escalating conflict with the Iran-backed Houthis in neighboring Yemen.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Why the era of cheap government debt is over
item.description: US debt has topped $40 trillion. How risky is the country's growing debt burden. And will investors keep funding Washington's deficits?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: US allies in Asia alarmed as think tank calls for pullback
item.description: Analysts warn that a US withdrawal from the western Pacific, as recently suggested by a think tank, would weaken deterrence and strengthen China's position.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: 'Woman, Life, Freedom' spirit lives on as Iran war drags on
item.description: The 2022 death of Jina Mahsa Amini in police custody triggered a resistance movement in Iran. Four years later, the Iranian regime endures — but so does the legacy of the "Woman, Life, Freedom" protests.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Netherlands: Suspected sabotage disrupts train services
item.description: A major outage has hit parts of the Dutch railway system after objects were found placed across lines, authorities say. The company responsible for rail infrastructure says it suspects deliberate wrongdoing.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Europe launches two climate observation satellites
item.description: The European Space Agency has put two satellites into orbit to take a closer look at the impact of climate change. One of them will focus particularly on plant life.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: EU seeks Arctic strategy amid growing power rivalry
item.description: Russia's aggression, Trump's threats against Greenland and the race for critical raw materials are pushing the Arctic to the top of Europe's agenda.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ukraine, Russia set for new round of US-mediated talks
item.description: New trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US could begin in October, according to Kyiv and Moscow. Few expect a breakthrough, but Ukraine is seeking a partial de-escalation to help it get through the winter.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Trump seeks halt to energy attacks by both Russia, Ukraine
item.description: Donald Trump, under fire for record US diesel prices, claims Russia and Ukraine have agreed to stop striking energy targets. Russia said nothing; Ukraine said "we expect specifics from our partners" on any such move.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Africa's richest man Dangote's IPO out of reach in Nigeria
item.description: Dangote seeks $1.6 billion from investors to finance a $14.3 billion expansion and thus double the oil refinery's capacity. The offer could give millions of Nigerians a stake in the company. But who can truly afford it?
item.dc:subject: World
